It fixes what Controller v0 is permitted to be before any line of it is written, so that the implementation mission cannot silently widen its own envelope.

fable_disposition.rule: FABLE_5_1 is authorized only as a conditional executor variant inside the existing Class B. It is not a new class, not a Class B default, and not a Class A substitute. It may be selected only when a machine-readable node/policy field explicitly permits it AND the task independently satisfies the Class-B authority envelope (frozen, well-specified implementation or remediation). Failing either condition, the Class B executor is SONNET.

policy_field.name: fableEligible
policy_field.rule: fableEligible defaults to false. Absence of the field is read as false, never as permission. Controller v0 may READ this field; Controller v0 may NEVER author, infer, default, promote or otherwise set fableEligible=true. Setting it true is an authoring act reserved to governed authority outside the controller.

eligibility_may_be_true_only_for: work where splitting materially increases total cost or risk
must_not_be_selected_merely_because: the model is perceived as stronger
fable_disposition.criterion_note: The objective is the marginal total cost per CORRECT closure, not per response, per token, or per apparent completion. A cheaper executor that produces a closure later reversed by audit is more expensive under this criterion, and a more expensive executor chosen without an interdependence justification is also more expensive under it.
fable_disposition.class_b_validation_requirements_preserve: Every existing Class-B empirical validation requirement in ODS_V1_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json model_executor_routing.classes.B remains applicable and unweakened, including validation_requirement (empirical validation on at least one governed implementation round using deterministic poststate evidence) and explicit_caution (model economy is NOT proof of adequacy). Selecting the Fable variant does not discharge, substitute for, or shortcut any of them, and the machine gates remain mandatory regardless of executor.

model_and_audit_routing.derivation_note: This block ROUTES against the frozen taxonomy in ODS_V1_AUTHORITY_v1.0.0.json; it does not redefine, restate or supersede it. executor_routing.CLASS_D: MACHINE — deterministic facts only (branch, HEAD, TREE, dirty state, hashes, scope, manifest ordering). No LLM.
executor_routing.CLASS_C: Lowest authorized bounded executor, or a deterministic script.
executor_routing.CLASS_B: Default SONNET. Conditional FABLE_5_1 variant only under mc1_disposition.fable_disposition.

audit_routing.self_certification_prohibition: Controller v0 cannot self-certify the boundary between MACHINE_ONLY, FOCUSED_OPUS and FULL_OPUS. It may route to a mode a node's authority already declares, and it may ESCALATE to a stricter mode, but it may never de-escalate, and it may never declare on its own judgment that a node needs less audit than its authority specifies. An undeclared or ambiguous boundary is a STOP (REQUIRED_INDEPENDENT_AUDIT or AUTHORITY_GAP), not a controller decision.

controller_v0_design.definition: Controller v0 is a thin deterministic node selector and router over machine gates that already exist in this repository. It selects the next authorized node, routes it to an executor class and an audit mode, invokes existing gates, classifies their output, and either advances or STOPs. It performs no semantic judgment that an existing gate already answers deterministically.

reuse_not_duplicate.rule: Controller v0 MUST reuse the following existing surfaces rather than reimplement, fork, wrap-with-divergent-semantics, or duplicate their logic. Every entry below was verified to exist in package.json scripts at BASE_SHA this session.

surfaces.role: changed-path classification against protected and allowed patterns
mission execution patterns (uellix-preflight, uellix-mission-loop, uellix-test-manifest, uellix-focused-reaudit, uellix-product-vertical, uellix-golden-e2e)

reuse_not_duplicate.duplication_prohibition: If Controller v0 needs a deterministic fact that one of the surfaces above already produces, it MUST invoke that surface and consume its output. Reimplementing the fact inside the controller is a design violation, because it creates a second source of truth that can silently diverge from the gate the rest of the program is audited against.

complexity_ceiling.rule: Controller v0 is exactly one script of at most 400 lines, plus its tests. It introduces no daemon, no long-running service, no database, no UI, no new orchestration framework, and no second state store. Program state is read from the existing registry and gates; the controller does not maintain a parallel copy of it. Exceeding any ceiling is a scope expansion requiring new authority, not a judgment call for the implementation mission.
complexity_ceiling.rationale: Every ceiling above exists because its violation would convert a citable, replayable, deterministic gate chain into an opaque stateful system. A second state store in particular reintroduces exactly the divergence class that ODS's machine gates were built to eliminate.

db_execution.rule: Controller v0 executes no database statement of any kind — no migration, no seed, no rehearsal, no read probe against a live cluster. Any node whose advancement would require database execution is a terminal STOP with DATABASE_AUTHORITY_REQUIRED. Enabling database execution requires separate governed authority (see the deferred P1A_FULL_BOOTSTRAP_STATUS node) and is explicitly out of scope for Controller v0.

state_model.disambiguation: These are CONTROLLER RUN states. They are distinct from, and do not redefine, the per-unit closure evidence vocabulary of ODS_PROGRAM_STATE_REGISTRY_v1.0.0.json (whose units are probed via json-field / paths-exist closedValues). The controller READS that registry's unit evidence; it does not rewrite the registry's semantics into its own run states, and it does not write to that registry.

stop_classes.origin: Established by the planning HPO and frozen here.
stop_classes.fail_closed_rule: Every stop class above halts the controller and escalates. The controller never reconciles, never infers past, and never downgrades a stop into a warning to keep advancing.

rerun_policy.rule: Only FLAKE_SUSPECTED may receive exactly one isolated autonomous rerun. Every other stop class is terminal on first occurrence.
rerun_policy.deterministic_repeat_rule: The same deterministic failure observed twice is a STOP (REPEATED_LOCAL_FAILURE). A second occurrence may never be reclassified as a flake to obtain another rerun.
rerun_policy.rationale: This is the anti-laundering rule: without it, any deterministic failure can be relabelled FLAKE_SUSPECTED indefinitely until it happens to pass, which converts a real defect into a green run.

controller_local_rule.requirement: The future ODS_CONTROLLER_POLICY MUST carry an explicit immutableByConvention[] array enumerating existing ODS authority, addendum and governance artifacts that Controller v0 must never mutate merely because ods:scope would accept an ordinary --allow covering them.
controller_local_rule.enforcement: When a controller-selected node targets any immutableByConvention entry for modification or deletion, Controller v0 MUST STOP with PROTECTED_SURFACE_CHANGE (or an equivalent fail-closed class). It must not proceed on the basis that ods:scope returned OK for that path.
controller_local_rule.defense_in_depth_note: This guard is ADDITIVE. It is a second, controller-local check layered on top of ods:scope, not a replacement for it and not a claim about it. ods:scope remains the authority for protected-surface classification; the controller simply refuses a class of mutation that ods:scope alone would not currently catch. A path may therefore be OK under ods:scope and still STOP the controller — that asymmetry is intentional.
controller_local_rule.precedence: If ods:scope and immutableByConvention disagree, the STRICTER outcome governs. The controller never uses an ods:scope OK to override immutableByConvention, and never uses immutableByConvention to authorize something ods:scope rejected.
